turns.content: For a pure two-qubit state alpha|00> + beta|01> + gamma|10> + delta|11>, state the separability criterion in terms of the determinant of the coefficient matrix [[alpha,beta],[gamma,delta]].
Explain why that determinant provides a decisive separability test for a pure two-qubit state and why an overall normalization factor does not affect whether it vanishes.
Apply the criterion to (a) (1/sqrt(30))(|00> + 2i|01> - 3|10> - 4i|11>) and (b) (1/5)(|00> + 2i|01> - 2|10> - 4i|11>). Is each state separable or entangled?
Now apply the same test to (c) (1/2)(|00> + |01> + |10> - |11>) and (d) (1/2)(|00> + |01> - |10> - |11>). Is each state separable or entangled?
Compare the four results and identify exactly which states are entangled.
Report alpha*delta - beta*gamma for each state so that the four classifications can be checked quantitatively.
Give the final entangled-state set and summarize how the determinant criterion establishes it.
